Using routine photoplethysmography (PPG), we extracted movement bouts from 65 preterm infants (47 without health complications, 18 with severe neurological conditions) across 50 days using a validated algorithm. Movement actigraphy was summarized using three novel metrics: (1) percent time moving per day across postmenstrual age, (2) daily distributions of movement durations quantified by power law exponents, and (3) ultradian movement cycles across 24 hours. While percent time moving did not change with age, power law exponents scaled linearly with age, indicating longer movements with maturation. Daily movement activity revealed 3-hour ultradian cycles corresponding to NICU feeding schedules, alongside an anticipatory rise in spontaneous motor activity before feeding. Infants with neurological complications, including two individual case studies, showed deviations in activity patterns when compared to uncomplicated infants. These results suggest that longitudinal movement tracking using routine sensors reveals systematic activity patterns and offers a scalable clinical tool for evaluation of health in this high-risk population.

title: FHIR-AgentEval: a modular sandbox for benchmarking clinical LLM agents with memory-augmented configurations
abstract: Healthcare data exchange increasingly relies on HL7 FHIR, but FHIR’s implementation complexity creates barriers for clinical workflows. Large language model (LLM) agents could bridge this gap by translating natural language requests into structured FHIR operations, yet their reliability remains unproven. We present FHIR-AgentEval, an extensible evaluation sandbox comprising 43 modular tasks for benchmarking LLM agents on realistic appointment management and genetic testing workflows. Each task executes against a resettable FHIR server with custom deterministic validation of both agent responses and resulting server state. We run an ablation study of five agent configurations, varying access to an on-demand FHIR R4 specifications server and long-term memory trained with or without specification grounding. Across four experimental settings, memory consistently improves task success and reduces strategic failures such as incorrect tool selection and resource-type confusion. On held-out tasks, the best memory configuration improves success by 9.1% over baseline, offering a potential pathway toward more robust clinical deployment.

title: Photography-based dental plaque detection and report generation among preschool children using PlaqueSAM
abstract: Dental plaque is the primary etiological factor for common oral diseases such as dental caries and gingivitis, particularly affecting susceptible populations including children. Preventing plaque-induced dental diseases in pediatric patients remains a global challenge as certain plaque regions are often missed during daily cleaning. Early detection and removal of plaque are essential but often difficult to achieve consistently. A routine monitoring tool that visualizes plaque accumulation on primary teeth could allow parents to actively track their children’s oral health, enabling timely prevention and intervention for dental caries and periodontal diseases. Inspired by these, we present PlaqueSAM, an automatic plaque detection system using intraoral photographs captured by smartphones. By uploading six images captured with the assistance of alignment overlays, PlaqueSAM can generate a comprehensive plaque detection report with visual references. PlaqueSAM was developed using 3402 prospectively collected intraoral photographs from 567 preschool children across 11 kindergartens in Hong Kong using a three-stage training strategy based on a multi-task learning paradigm. The performance of PlaqueSAM was quantitatively evaluated on 81 children, achieving sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 76.58, 82.47, and 79.60%, respectively. These findings suggest that PlaqueSAM may support future plaque screening workflows without requiring disclosing agents or plastic retractors typically used by dental professionals, although home-based use requires further validation under real-world user-operated conditions. With further real-world validation, PlaqueSAM may support dynamic monitoring of children’s daily plaque accumulation and cleaning, thereby contributing to the advancement of teledentistry and promoting children’s oral health remotely, conveniently, and at a lower cost.

title: An agentic AI system for multi-framework communication coding
abstract: Clinical communication is central to patient outcomes, yet large-scale annotation of patient–provider conversations remains labor-intensive, inconsistent, and difficult to scale. Existing large language model (LLM)–based approaches typically rely on single-task systems with limited robustness across communication frameworks and clinical domains. In this study, we developed MOSAIC, a M ulti-framew O rk S tructured Agentic AI system for scalable Clinical C ommunication coding. MOSAIC combines dynamically few-shot prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a LangGraph-based multi-agent workflow for planning, annotation, and verification. Performance was evaluated against gold-standard annotations produced by trained human coders. MOSAIC was developed on 54 annotated transcripts and evaluated on 120 transcripts spanning rheumatology and obstetrics/gynecology (OB/GYN). On the evaluation set, MOSAIC achieved an overall weighted F1 score of 95.6%. Performance was highest in rheumatology (F1 = 95.9%) and strongest for bias and patient behaviors categories (F1 = 96.4% and 96.1%, respectively). These results demonstrate the potential of multi-framework AI systems for reliable clinical communication analysis.

title: From authoring to editing: a competency framework for trainee use of ambient AI clinical documentation
abstract: Ambient AI has spread through clinical settings faster than curricula can adapt, shifting trainee documentation from authoring to editing notes. Authoring historically honed clinical reasoning for trainees, yet medical education is not prepared to develop the editing task now replacing it. We define this task as a teachable competency with four domains - error detection, clinical reconciliation, independent generation, and trust calibration - and describe how simulation can teach them.

title: AI-based hourly prediction of emergency department demand integrating social determinants of health
abstract: Emergency department (ED) crowding is associated with delayed treatment and increased mortality, and proactive staffing requires reliable short-term demand forecasts. Most operational models rely on temporal or weather patterns but may insufficiently capture underlying population vulnerability. We evaluated whether community-level social determinants of health (SDoH) improve the prediction of near-term ED demand compared with weather factors using XGBOOST, and developed an interpretable model to inform resource allocation. The study included 213,138 encounters aggregated into 22,883 hourly observations at a tertiary teaching hospital in Wuhan, China. Neighbourhoods differed markedly in age structure and diagnostic profiles, indicating heterogeneous healthcare needs across the catchment area. Models incorporating dynamic SDoH features consistently outperformed those using weather variables alone. Overall, the composite model achieved the best performance with an RMSE of 3.48 visits per hour, an MAE of 2.62 visits per hour, and an R ² of 0.68. Mean absolute prediction errors were approximately 2 to 3 patients per hour across scenarios, suggesting practical utility for short-term staffing and capacity planning. The study indicates that community-level social vulnerability may provide more informative signals than weather conditions for anticipating short-term ED demand. Integrating SDoH-informed forecasts into hospital operations may enable earlier staffing adjustments and help mitigate crowding-related risks.

title: Technology-Enabled Hospital Discharge: Consolidated Framework of Implementation Research-Informed Qualitative Study of Stakeholder Perspectives on Digital Solutions
abstract: Hospital discharge is a complex, time-consuming process that requires coordination across multiple stakeholders. Technology-enabled solutions may improve this process, but their implementation depends on alignment with user needs, workflows, and care contexts. We explored stakeholder perspectives on six candidate digital solutions for hospital discharge as part of a wider service improvement project. We interviewed forty-three purposively sampled healthcare workers, operations staff, patients, and caregivers. We introduced participants to ward-based teleconsultation, smart glasses, AI bots, medication collection boxes, digital discharge documentation, and AI-assisted discharge summary drafting, and explored perceived value, risks and implementation requirements. We analysed the data using a hybrid deductive–inductive approach informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Participants described discharge as poorly communicated, lacking transparency, and often prolonged. We identified eleven subthemes under the five CFIR domains. Participants viewed technologies more favourably when they could see practical value, when the technology was familiar from other contexts, and when it could integrate with existing workflows while preserving the relational aspects of care. Concerns centred on safety, privacy, equity, workflow disruption, burden, and loss of human interaction. Successful implementation requires a clear value proposition, workflow integration, stakeholder co-design, and early attention to training, governance, accountability, and equity.

title: Realizing the value of the divergence event in clinical human-AI interaction
abstract: When a clinician’s judgment and AI output diverge, what each side contributed disappears with the decision, because current interfaces capture the outcome and not the interaction. We propose that the clinician-AI interaction requires its own account and describe how divergence can be made visible. Making the divergence event visible supports transparent patient communication, better grounds moral responsibility, may mitigate liability, and reframes divergence as clinical AI’s highest-signal moment.

title: Model-dependent prompt effects challenge reliable deployment of medical LLMs in traditional Chinese medicine
abstract: Although contemporary large language models (LLMs) have achieved satisfactory results in Western medical knowledge, their performance on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains underexplored, and the determinants of performance variation are poorly understood. We evaluated 16 LLMs under seven prompt strategies on 475 questions from the 2025 Taiwan national TCM licensing examination, a public benchmark of TCM knowledge. Without prompt engineering, accuracy ranged from 35.4% to 85.9%, with approximately half passing. Among the evaluated model versions, adjusted accuracy differed substantially when models were grouped by family (for example, Claude-family models, 84% vs. GPT-4, 43%); these family-grouped comparisons were descriptive because only 16 individual models were evaluated. Paired prompt analyses showed modest average absolute effects, ranging from a 2.03-percentage-point decrease with implicit CoT to a 3.04-percentage-point increase with explicit CoT. However, prompt–model interactions produced substantial model-level divergence: prompt optimization reversed failing performance in one model (87.4% vs. 49.7%) while reducing accuracy in others. No single prompt strategy yielded consistent benefits across the evaluated models. Among five selected lower-performing models evaluated under explicit CoT prompting, misunderstanding of foundational TCM concepts was the most frequent error. These findings indicate that reliable LLM deployment in TCM requires empirical validation of both model choice and prompt strategy: model selection strongly shapes baseline capability, while prompt-model interactions can materially alter performance.

title: Multidimensional continuous glucose monitoring metrics enable digital risk stratification across the diabetes spectrum
abstract: Although continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides high-dimensional data, the usefulness of multimodal and diurnal glycemic profiles for disease characterization and risk stratification remains unknown. Here, in the iCanNet cohort of 90,757 participants, we examined the associations of 48 CGM-derived metrics with prediabetes, T2D, and T1D, compared to normoglycemia. We further employed Gaussian Mixture Model to define glycemic phenotypes and established digital glycemic risk score (DGRS) to quantify complication risks in T2D. Participants with prediabetes, T2D, or T1D exhibited distinct CGM signatures compared to normoglycemic individuals (all P < 0.001). Integration of top five metrics significantly improved diabetes classification, and calibration analyses showed agreement between predicted and observed risks. Four glycemic phenotypes were identified in T2D, with sustained hyperglycemia associated with a 59% increased risk of acute complications, and high glycemic variability associated with 75% and 41% higher risks of acute and chronic complications, respectively. The DGRS identified residual risk among patients achieving time in range ≥70%, reclassifying 25.0% and 22.3% of these individuals to high-risk groups for acute and chronic complications, respectively. In summary, this study revealed distinct CGM-derived signatures across diabetes statuses and established a multimodal framework for identifying high-risk individuals with T2D who may be overlooked by conventional biomarkers.

title: AEGIS: an operational infrastructure for post-market governance of adaptive medical AI under US and EU regulatory frameworks
abstract: Medical AI requires governance preserving safety during continuous improvement. FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and EU post-market surveillance address iterative updates but lack operational tooling. We present AEGIS, an internal governance and post-market-monitoring infrastructure designed to support the documentation of predetermined governance pathways for PCCP and Medical Devices Regulation alignment. AEGIS comprises dataset assimilation and retraining, model monitoring, and conditional decision-making modules. It utilizes a four-category taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) and an independent ALARM signal. Instantiating AEGIS for sepsis prediction (PhysioNet) and brain-tumor segmentation (BraTS) exercised all decision categories, successfully routing failures to the critical REJECT + ALARM state (no deployable model; released model at risk). On real cross-site data, drift detection ROC-AUC rose from 0.82 to 1.00, reliably triggering near 500-patient batches with zero false alarms. This proof-of-concept utilizes illustrative clinical models; drift scoring quantifies covariate shift only, leaving concept drift for future work.

title: Development of a scoring system via an interpretable end-to-end neural network for prognostic stratification of patients with advanced melanoma
abstract: We created an interpretable end-to-end neural network (ScoreNet) which can be used to develop an easy-to-implement scoring system for risk stratification. We applied it to data from 2711 patients with advanced melanoma across 5 trials that supported new drug approvals and developed a scoring system for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The scoring system was then validated in two separate trials. This score is a weighted summation based on eight baseline features (sum of longest diameter for all target lesions, lactate dehydrogenase, systemic immune inflammation index, hemoglobin, ECOG performance status, liver metastasis, pulse rate, and PD-L1 immunohistochemistry status). Using the score, patients can be classified into low, moderate, or high-risk categories of reduced OS and PFS. Risk stratification was demonstrated for patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, chemotherapy, CTLA-4 inhibitors, BRAF or MEK inhibitors, and their combinations. ScoreNet-based risk stratification can be a new tool for clinical research/practice.

title: Exploring PET and MRI brain networks across healthy controls, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: This study aimed to characterize population-level and individual-level metabolic and radiomics-derived structural brain networks across healthy controls (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) using multimodal PET and MRI. A total of 651 participants with both [ 18 F]FDG PET and MRI were retrospectively included, with an external cohort of 45 participants used for validation. Thirty-two AD-relevant regions of interest were retained as network nodes and characterized using PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and a selected MRI radiomics descriptor. Population-level networks were constructed using probability density function-based similarity with Jensen–Shannon divergence, and individualized perturbation networks were derived relative to an HC reference. Network-derived features were evaluated for prediction. Both SUVR-based and radiomics-based networks showed distinct patterns in MCI and AD compared with HC. Fused network features improved discrimination compared with either modality alone, achieving one-vs-rest AUCs of 0.894 [0.868–0.917] for HC, 0.888 [0.862–0.912] for AD, and 0.814 [0.783–0.844] for MCI. These findings indicate graded network disorganization across the HC–MCI–AD spectrum and support multimodal prediction.

title: A “growth mindset of mental health” intervention increases the likelihood of initiating self-help on a mental health app: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Mental health apps hold potential to improve access to treatment, but engagement remains low. One barrier may be the belief that mental health cannot be meaningfully improved. In a randomized controlled trial ( N = 252), we examined whether a brief growth-mindset-of-mental-health intervention—portraying mental health as improvable, not fixed—can initiate mental health app engagement among people with mental health needs. Participants completed baseline well-being measures (stress, anxiety and depression, and positive mental well-being) and were randomly assigned to the growth-mindset-of-mental-health or active control condition. Over the subsequent three months, we tracked whether they re-engaged with the app overall (i.e., completed at least a second self-help feature), and with features categorized as low-, moderate-, and high-intensity. Analyses revealed that participants in the growth-mindset condition (vs. control) with poorer baseline mental well-being (i.e., higher stress, anxiety and depressive symptoms, and lower positive mental well-being) were significantly more likely to show repeat app engagement. Moreover, those with higher anxiety and depressive symptoms were more likely to show repeat engagement with moderate-intensity features, while those experiencing higher stress and lower positive mental well-being were more likely to do so with both low- and moderate-intensity features. Together, these findings demonstrate the benefits of the growth-mindset intervention for successful initiation of self-help on a mental health app. Trial Registration: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07071311) on July 25, 2025.

title: Current status and future outlook of artificial intelligence and automation in intravenous infusion systems
abstract: The combination of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and wearable biosensors is transforming healthcare by allowing continuous, real-time monitoring and more intelligent clinical decision-making. This review explores AI-driven monitoring, smart intravenous (IV) infusion automation, and wearable biosensors, and proposes Intelligent IV Automation and Smart Patient Synchronization (INFUSYNC), a conceptual framework synchronizing monitoring, automated fluid delivery, and predictive analytics. The literature shows meaningful progress: wearables increasingly support non-contact monitoring with near clinical-grade accuracy for select parameters, while infusion pumps with dose-error-reduction and AI-assisted decision support are reported to improve delivery precision and safety. Predictive models further support early detection of physiological decline. Progress remains uneven, however: most AI-enabled infusion systems are prototype-stage, closed-loop control remains rare, and interoperability, data security, and privacy remain underdeveloped. Future systems will need compatible, security-by-design, clinically validated, feedback-controlled architectures. Overall, this review outlines a clear but early-stage trajectory toward integrated smart-health environments for IV therapy.

title: Author Correction: Large language models are powerful electronic health record encoders
Electronic health record developer adherence to federal AI risk transparency requirements
abstract: We evaluated electronic health record developer compliance with federal transparency requirements for AI-enabled predictive decision support interventions. Developers are required to publicly report on risk analysis, mitigation, governance, and on eight other attributes. Across 35 developers, reporting was inconsistent and often incomplete, with substantial variation in structure and detail, yet all developers were certified as meeting the requirements. Results suggest a need for standardized reporting and more rigorous certification review.

title: From research to clinical practice: Expert consensus on Neuroimaging AI tools for the Memory clinic (Neuro-AIM)
abstract: Although AI tools for neuroimaging show considerable promise in the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of neurodegenerative disorders, their uptake in memory clinics has been limited. A key barrier is lack of consensus on their effective design and implementation. Here we establish expert consensus on the specific goals, usage and challenges of AI tools for neuroimaging in the memory clinic using a Delphi process. Sixteen experts from clinical, academic, and industry backgrounds participated in three rounds of questionnaires, coordinated by the Imaging Working Group of the Deep Dementia Phenotyping (DEMON) network, with support from a patient and public involvement representative. Consensus was reached on eight statements covering four themes: purpose, quality, interactions with clinicians and memory clinics, and privacy and ethics. Implementation of these recommendations will further the adoption of AI neuroimaging tools from research to clinical practice, improving diagnostic and care pathways for patient benefit.

title: Sequence models reveal diagnosis accumulation pathways beyond comorbidity burden in population-scale hospital data
abstract: Aging trajectories vary among individuals of similar age and disease burden. Comorbidity indices, e.g. the Elixhauser index, aggregate recorded conditions into a single score, but discard the timing, sequence, and pace of morbidity accumulation. Here we ask whether longitudinal hospital diagnosis histories contain information beyond age, sex, and comorbidity burden, and where it is concentrated. Using 13 years of Austrian inpatient data covering 7.4 million patients, we trained a visit-level contrastive transformer to encode diagnosis sequences and inter-admission timing into patient-history embeddings. In a downstream cohort of 1.7 million individuals, the embedding model improved prediction of in-hospital death over the Elixhauser-based comorbidity model, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.879 versus 0.866 (AUC gain = 0.0132, 95% CI 0.0118–0.0144). Across 130 incident ICD-10 disease-block outcomes, the embedding model had higher AUC for 93 outcomes, with a modest median gain of 0.006. Gains were concentrated in mental, musculoskeletal, nervous system, and metabolic disorders. We then evaluated event-free survival, defined as remaining alive without accumulating a second unrecorded ICD-10 disease block. The embedding model achieved an AUC of 0.726 versus 0.722 for the comorbidity model. However, among patients with similar age, sex, and comorbidity-model risk, those assigned high residual risk had 127–181 fewer event-free days over five years and observed event rates comparable to low-residual-risk patients more than a decade older. Together, these findings link the embedding’s signal to the breadth, recency, and pace of prior disease accumulation.

title: From compliance to competence: a multi-level model for AI governance in undergraduate medical education
abstract: AI's fast-paced irruption in medicine and education has challenged undergraduate medical colleges, with institutions documenting policies emphasizing immediate conduct restrictions, while strategic oversight, infrastructure and evaluation remain less consistently developed. We propose a multi-level framework for AI governance in undergraduate medical education based on accountability, competence and co-responsibility across institutions, educators and students, designed to turn a fast-evolving technology from a threat into an opportunity for collective progress.

title: FedFound: Federated Foundation Model for GI endoscopy imaging
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is essential for identifying abnormalities and enabling early diagnosis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and facilitating timely clinical intervention. While deep learning has shown promise in supporting GI diagnostics, most models require carefully labeled datasets that are costly to acquire and limited in scope. Foundation models offer a paradigm shift by learning general-purpose representations that can be adapted for diverse tasks, addressing data scarcity and variability. However, training such models on medical imaging data remains challenging due to privacy regulations, security concerns, and fragmented digital infrastructures that prevent centralized data aggregation, even as hospitals collectively generate vast amounts of endoscopic data. To overcome these barriers, we propose a federated learning (FL) framework for GI foundation models, allowing data to remain local while collaboratively training a shared model. We extensively evaluate multiple FL algorithms under both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings across three clinically relevant downstream tasks-classification, detection, and segmentation. We further evaluate our framework with a larger number of clients and across diverse pretraining strategies to assess its scalability and robustness. Our results demonstrate consistent performance gains, underscoring the potential of Federated Foundation Models to enable clinically validated AI applications and support secure, regulation-compliant deployment in real-world gastroendoscopy practice.

title: Characterizing time-of-day physical activity patterns across cognitive trajectories in older adults: a longitudinal cohort study
abstract: Declining cognitive function is a growing health challenge, yet how cognitive decline influences time-of-day physical activity (PA) patterns remains underexplored. Among cognitively unimpaired participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study, we modeled general and domain-specific cognitive trajectories and related them to accelerometry-derived PA a median of 8.2 years later in 811 participants (mean baseline age 73.1 years) using function-on-scalar and multivariable regression. Slower cognitive decline was associated with more favorable midday PA (10 AM–3 PM), including higher movement volume, less sedentary time, fewer interruptions to active periods, and greater activity variability. In adjusted linear regression models, associations with PA patterns derived from a window as short as 11 AM-1 PM were comparable to those with 24-hour measures. The executive function trajectory exhibited the strongest associations with PA patterns, and over the longest period of the day; the language trajectory showed non-linear associations, and the peak association for the memory trajectory with PA occurred in the late morning (10:30–11:30 AM). Associations between cognitive decline and activity variability were stronger than for other PA metrics. Our findings highlight the potential of PA patterns, particularly activity variability, as a non-invasive way to help monitor cognitive decline before clinical impairment emerges.

title: Implementation and effectiveness of a smartphone app targeted at improving physicians adherence to antimicrobial treatment guidelines
abstract: The effectiveness of mHealth interventions for improving antimicrobial guideline adherence remains insufficiently understood in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated a context-adapted smartphone Standard Treatment Guideline (STG) app designed to improve physicians’ adherence to antimicrobial treatment guidelines in Ethiopia. A type 1 hybrid effectiveness–implementation cluster-randomized trial was conducted in 20 hospitals randomized to a smartphone app plus training or paper-based guidelines and retrospectively registered (PACTR202504495116733). The primary outcome was guideline-adherent prescribing, defined as correct antibiotic selection, dose, frequency, and duration when treatment was indicated, or appropriately documented non-prescribing when antibiotics were not indicated across 1433 patient charts. Secondary outcomes included overall antibiotic use and broad-spectrum antibiotic use. Guideline adherence improved by 26.7 percentage points in crude difference-in-differences analysis, and the adjusted intervention-by-endline effect showed higher odds of guideline-adherent prescribing (aOR 3.89; 95% CI: 1.96–7.73). Overall, antibiotic use declined from 96.9% to 82.2% in the intervention arm. In a post-hoc sensitivity analysis using all eligible charts, broad-spectrum antibiotic use declined from 83.9 to 57.5%. These findings support the potential value of a multicomponent intervention combining an offline STG app with training and implementation support for improving guideline-concordant antimicrobial prescribing; however, the independent contribution of the mobile application cannot be determined.

title: An artificial intelligence framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
abstract: Phenotyping is fundamental to rare disease diagnosis, but manually curating structured phenotypes from clinical notes is labor intensive and difficult to scale. Existing artificial intelligence (AI) approaches optimize individual components of phenotyping but generally do not operationalize the full workflow of extracting features from clinical text, standardizing them to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms, and prioritizing rare disease-relevant HPO terms. We developed RARE-PHENIX, an end-to-end AI framework for rare disease phenotyping that integrates large language model-based phenotype extraction, ontology-grounded standardization to HPO terms, and supervised ranking of HPO terms. We trained RARE-PHENIX using data from 2671 patients across 11 Undiagnosed Diseases Network clinical sites, and externally validated it on 16,357 real-world clinical notes from 143 patients at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Our findings suggest RARE-PHENIX generates structured, prioritized HPO terms highly concordant with clinician curation, demonstrates potential downstream disease-prioritization signal, and may support human-in-the-loop rare disease phenotyping in real-world settings.

title: TrajOnco: a multi-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi-cancer early detection
abstract: Accurate estimation of cancer risk from longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) could support earlier detection and improved care, but modeling such complex patient trajectories remains challenging. We present TrajOnco, a training-free, multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework designed for scalable multi-cancer early detection. Using a chain-of-agents architecture with long-term memory, TrajOnco performs temporal reasoning over sequential clinical events to generate patient-level summaries, evidence-linked rationales, and predicted risk scores. We evaluated TrajOnco on de-identified Truveta EHR data across 15 cancer types using matched case-control cohorts, predicting risk of cancer diagnosis at 1 year. In zero-shot evaluation, TrajOnco achieved AUROCs of 0.64–0.80, performing comparably to supervised machine learning in a lung cancer benchmark while demonstrating better temporal reasoning than single-agent LLMs. The multi-agent design also enabled effective temporal reasoning with smaller-capacity models such as GPT-4.1-mini. The groundedness of TrajOnco’s output was supported by human evaluation. Furthermore, TrajOnco’s interpretable reasoning outputs can be aggregated to reveal population-level risk patterns that align with established clinical knowledge. These findings highlight the potential of multi-agent LLMs to execute interpretable temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHRs, advancing both scalable multi-cancer early detection and clinical insight generation.

title: Solving operating room scheduling problems using large language model based multi-agent architecture
abstract: Efficient operating room scheduling is a complex task due to the diversity of surgical types, high patient demand, and limited hospital resources. Since OR operations account for a substantial share of hospital costs, effective scheduling solutions are critical. Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems offer new opportunities to support optimization for this problem. This study evaluates an LLM-based multi-agent framework for generating and refining optimization code for OR scheduling. Leveraging iterative collaboration among specialized agents, the proposed iterative multi-agent (IMA) framework consistently outperformed both single-agent and traditional multi-agent baselines. Across 10 LLMs and 35 scenarios, IMA achieved an average feasible schedule rate of 82.91%, compared with 65.59% and 52.53% for the baselines. Experiments on 1050 synthetic cases and three real OR datasets further showed that IMA-generated code produced solutions close to those of expert-written mixed-integer programming models, while a case study of hospital as-is schedules demonstrated improvements in OR utilization and overtime reduction. These results suggest that LLM-based multi-agent systems can provide a practical and effective approach for OR scheduling optimization.

title: Postoperative CT habitat fusion model predicts prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy
abstract: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NAIC) has been widely adopted for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, reliable tools for postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) risk stratification remain lacking. We developed and validated a habitat radiomics–clinicopathological fusion model, termed the Neoadjuvant Lung Joint Clustering (NeoLung-JC) model, for postoperative DFS stratification and prediction in patients with NSCLC who underwent surgery after NAIC. The model integrates dual-sequence CT-derived tumor habitat heterogeneity scores with key clinicopathological factors. The habitat heterogeneity scores were extracted from the tumor core and peripheral regions using a joint clustering approach. In a multicenter cohort of 508 patients, the NeoLung-JC model showed favorable and consistent predictive performance, achieving a concordance index of 0.750 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.680–0.807) in the external validation cohort. The model significantly stratified patients into high-, medium-, and low-risk DFS groups, with clearly separated Kaplan–Meier survival curves across all cohorts ( P < 0.0001). Its prognostic performance exceeded that of conventional clinicopathological indicators, including clinical TNM (cTNM) stage, post-treatment pathological TNM (ypTNM) stage, and pathological response. By integrating dual-sequence CT-derived tumor spatial heterogeneity with clinical risk characteristics, the NeoLung-JC model may provide a useful supplementary approach for individualized postoperative prognostic assessment in patients with NSCLC undergoing surgery after NAIC.

title: A generalist model for diverse text-guided medical image synthesis
abstract: Deep learning requires extensive data to achieve robust performance. However, data availability is often restricted in medicine due to patient privacy concerns. Synthetic data from medical image generative models present a possible solution to these challenges. Unfortunately, many models are often task-specific or trained on private datasets, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this, we introduce MediSyn: an open-access, generalist, text-guided latent diffusion model. MediSyn can generate images across 6 medical specialties and 10 imaging modalities, while being trained exclusively on public data. Our study provides several key contributions using MediSyn. First, we demonstrate that a generalist model can generate images of comparable quality to task-specific models across multiple specialties. Second, we show that this generalist approach is more computationally efficient than a suite of task-specific models. Third, we establish that a generalist model can produce realistic, text-aligned images across visually and medically distinct modalities. Fourth, we empirically demonstrate that these synthetic images are visually distinct from real images used in training. Finally, we show that a generalist model can produce images that improve classifier performance in data-limited settings across multiple specialties. Altogether, our findings highlight the potential of generalist image generative models to accelerate medical algorithmic research and development.

title: Effectiveness of ecological momentary interventions for patients with cancer: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Symptom burden and impaired quality of life (QoL) are major challenges for patients with cancer. Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) offer real-time, context-sensitive, and personalized support, enabling more precise management of patient needs. To explore the effectiveness of EMIs in improving symptoms and QoL in patients with cancer, a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. Following PRISMA 2020, a comprehensive search was conducted in nine databases from inception to December 8, 2025. The RoB 2 tool and GRADE were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence, respectively. The R (version 4.4.1) and the “meta” package were used for statistical analysis. A total of 17 studies involving 4,160 randomized participants were included. The results suggested that EMIs may improve depression in patients with cancer, but were not associated with significant improvements in fatigue, pain severity, pain interference, sleep disturbance, anxiety, or QoL. Given the limited certainty and robustness of the available evidence, further adequately powered, allocation-concealed randomized controlled trials with blinded outcome assessment, where feasible, are needed to strengthen the evidence base for EMIs in oncology care.

title: Automated differentiation for parkinsonism using clinical structural MRI: A multicenter study
abstract: Multimodal research-grade magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans show potential for differentiating Parkinson’s disease (PD) from multiple system atrophy (MSA), but clinical translation is limited by cost, acquisition time, and processing burden. Here, we developed a T1-weighted structural MRI-based machine learning model to differentiate Parkinsonism and generalized it to routine anisotropic 2D clinical MRI. Using a multicenter cohort of 969 participants, we employed a hierarchical discovery–verification–translation framework. While a multimodal benchmark model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.98, our streamlined unimodal T1-Top20 model achieved an AUROC of 0.93 for multiclass discrimination (healthy controls, PD, MSA). For PD vs MSA, the frozen T1-Top20 model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.88 in the external research-grade cohort ( n = 227) and identified 19 of 25 who phenoconverted from idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) to PD. Importantly, the generalized model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.84 in the clinical-MRI cohort (2D T1, n = 303), supporting its potential for clinical translation.

title: Sycophantic AI, critical-feedback tolerance, and the case for productive friction in medical training
abstract: Concerns about generative AI in medical training often focus on eroded reasoning and deskilling. Such competence-based accounts are incomplete. We identify a neglected casualty: critical-feedback tolerance (CFT), the capacity to receive disconfirming evaluative feedback and remain productively engaged. Affirmation-optimized systems may lower CFT undetectably, surfacing only under authentic critique. This conceptual Perspective defines CFT, differentiates it from six established constructs, specifies measurable facets, and states explicit refutation conditions.

title: A multi-stage validation framework for trustworthy large-scale clinical information extraction using large language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show promise for extracting clinically meaningful information from unstructured health records, yet real-world deployment is constrained by limited scalable, trustworthy validation approaches. Conventional evaluation relies on annotation-intensive reference standards and incomplete structured data, limiting population-scale use. We propose a multi-stage validation framework for LLM-based clinical information extraction that enables rigorous assessment under weak supervision by integrating complementary validation strategies. The framework combines prompt calibration, rule-based filtering, semantic grounding, judge-LLM evaluation, expert review, and predictive validity analysis to quantify uncertainty without exhaustive manual annotation. We applied this framework to extract substance use disorder (SUD) diagnoses across 11 substance categories from 919,783 clinical notes. Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported or structurally implausible. For high-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert. Using judge evaluations as references, the primary LLM achieved an F1 score of 0.80. LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines. By unifying complementary validation strategies, this work presents a generalizable human-in-the-loop framework for establishing the trustworthiness of LLM-based clinical information extraction at scale while minimizing the need for exhaustive manual annotation.

title: GWDRO-Lung: Gromov–Wasserstein distributionally robust learning for calibrated pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction across imaging cohorts
abstract: Low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) screening detects pulmonary nodules whose malignancy risk must be triaged, yet deep-learning risk models often lose both accuracy and calibration when transferred to a different scanner, protocol, or population. We developed GWDRO-Lung, a chest CT framework that treats cross-cohort transfer as a coupled problem of structural mismatch, distributional instability, and calibration. A weight-shared three-dimensional encoder with embedded acquisition metadata summarizes each cohort as a relation matrix over learned prototypes; cohort geometries are aligned to a shared Gromov–Wasserstein barycenter; and a distributionally robust, calibration-aware risk head estimates malignancy, with the residual alignment error setting a cohort-specific robustness radius. The model was developed on 1842 pulmonary nodules from LIDC-IDRI, organized into three acquisition-defined cohorts, and validated externally on 618 nodules from the independent LNDb cohort, with leave-one-cohort-out, protocol-shift, size-stratified, and decision-curve analyses. Relative to the strongest recent imaging baseline, external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve improved from 0.857 to 0.878, external expected calibration error fell from 0.106 to 0.066, worst-cohort AUC rose from 0.829 to 0.851, and net benefit was higher across triage-relevant thresholds. Prospective, pathology-confirmed validation is required before clinical use.

title: Large language models for depression assessment from brief daily diaries
abstract: Closely tracking changes in depression is important for clinical research and practice. However, intensive longitudinal depression assessment relies on self-report surveys that have major limitations. Scoring depression from natural language with large language models (LLMs) could resolve these shortcomings. This study tested the validity of depression rated by LLMs from daily video diaries. We studied 108 participants selected for mental health treatment status (45% in treatment). Participants completed a clinical interview and 14-21 days of depression surveys and video diaries. Daily depression scores were estimated by LLMs from diary transcripts. LLM ratings converged with self-report depression within-person ( r = .45;95% CrI[.40, .49]) and when averaged across days for an overall depression score ( r = .61;95% CrI[.43,.75]). Averaged LLM ratings correlated with depression symptom severity ascertained by clinical interview ( r = .53;95% CrI[.35, .68]). LLM-rated depression and self-report had similar profiles of associations with daily functioning variables (profile r = .98 within-person; r = .94 between-person). Multivariable regression results showed LLM ratings predicted daily functioning variables (partial \(\beta s\) =|.12 | - | .28 | ) and interview-rated depression (partial \(\beta\) =.33;95% CrI[.07, .58]) over and above self-reports, suggesting LLMs capture clinically-relevant information that self-reports miss. Findings establish a strong foundation for a depression assessment approach that addresses shortcomings of self-reports while satisfying the unique demands of intensive longitudinal monitoring.

title: AI-supported first consultation preparation in oncology: a real-world clinical usability study
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) may support clinicians by facilitating information management, but their usability in real-world oncology practice remains understudied. This study evaluated the workflow performance of Artificial Intelligence-based First Consultation Preparation (AI-FCP), generating structured summaries from unstructured clinical documentation, co-created with end users. In a prospective single‑group pre‑post design, nine clinicians completed a person-level baseline, followed by 33 consultations with AI-FCP. Case numbers varied by clinic scheduling and enrollment timing, potentially introducing survivorship bias. Usability was evaluated using validated questionnaires and study-specific instruments. Post AI-FCP, overall perceived workload (NASA-TLX) was 28.9% lower than baseline (Hodges-Lehmann estimate difference −12.3; 95% CI –21.7 to –3.3), with self-reported average time savings of 3.26 min (SD = 2.65) per case. Preparation succeeded in 84.9% of consultations; 63.6% of summaries were complete. These exploratory findings suggest clinicians perceived lower workload and reported improved workflow efficiency with AI-FCP. Further research is needed to determine generalizability.

title: Reinforcement learning for repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation protocol selection in treatment-resistant depression
abstract: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), including intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), is an established treatment for treatment-resistant depression, but clinicians lack evidence-based guidance for session-level choices among stimulation type, intensity, and laterality. In this study, we investigated whether a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm trained on routine clinical data could recommend session-level rTMS protocols associated with greater symptom improvement using electronic health record data from 1609 adults treated with rTMS between January 2023 and June 2025 across 19 clinic groups. Among 370 patients from held-out clinics, treatment decisions matching algorithm recommendations were associated with 0.788 points greater next-session Patient Health Questionnaire-9 improvement than treatments that differed (95% CI: 0.634–0.940). Following every recommendation was projected to produce 3.22 points of additional improvement (95% CI: 2.72–3.75). These findings suggest RL can find treatment patterns associated with greater next-session improvement and potentially meaningful improvement accumulated across a treatment episode.

title: A generalizable deep learning model for predicting opioid use disorder using language modeling for cross-EHR data harmonization
abstract: The opioid use disorder (OUD) epidemic in the United States has been a major public health crisis. We developed OUD-REY ( OUD R isk E valuator at 1 Y ear) - a deep learning model that uses longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from the All of Us research program to predict risk of OUD at one year for patients with an opioid prescription. On internal validation, OUD-REY achieved an AUROC of 91.2% and AUPRC of 77.0%. We leveraged a pretrained language model to accommodate thousands of unseen, out-of-vocabulary clinical features in a patient’s longitudinal EHR history. We externally validated our model on a new dataset released by All of Us that was temporally separated from our development set and on a dataset containing ~6 million patients from medical centers of the Veterans Affairs (VA) nationwide over a span of 20 years. On external validation, our model had an AUROC and AUPRC of 86.4% and 23.1% (OUD prevalence of 2.9%), respectively, on our temporally separated All of Us validation set. It had an AUROC and AUPRC of 85.5% and 19.5% (OUD prevalence of 3.5%), respectively, on the VA dataset. Our fairness auditing showed that the model was generally fair for patients with different genders, race, and ethnic backgrounds. This model may potentially improve prevention and care of OUD.

title: Extending synthetic medical education: generating OSCE cases with LLMs
abstract: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are central to competency-based medical education, yet high-quality case development is resource-intensive. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable solution, but comprehensive OSCE case generation, including components such as candidate instructions, standardized patient scripts, and examiner marking schemes, is underexplored. We developed an LLM-based tool to generate complete OSCE stations. Three board-certified internists evaluated 24 generated cases across eight internal medicine diagnoses and three learner levels using a 12-item Likert instrument. Ratings were high across all domains; communication behaviors (4.64/5), EPA alignment (4.62/5), and overall value (4.61/5) performed best; guideline concordance scored lowest (4.24/5) with the greatest rater disagreement. As a feasibility study, these findings establish that whole, schema-validated OSCE stations can be generated from a single structured call at a quality experts rate as acceptable, while also identifying guideline concordance and difficult calibration as the domains most requiring faculty oversight -- providing reproducible infrastructure for, but not yet evidence of, effective EPA-aligned OSCE development.

title: Physiologic digital twins for decision support in multi-day ex vivo organ perfusion
abstract: Many potentially recoverable donor livers are discarded because current paradigms prioritize preservation and viability assessment over prolonged stabilization and rehabilitation. Multi-day normothermic ex vivo perfusion creates a therapeutic window but shifts the challenge from sustaining circulation to interpreting evolving physiologic trajectories without native homeostatic regulation. We propose physiologic digital twins that integrate mechanistic and statistical models to estimate organ state and support decision-making during ex vivo perfusion.

title: Expertise modulates automation bias and sentinel behavior in human–AI collaborative diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum
abstract: Medical AI is often validated under an additive assumption that algorithmic sensitivity and clinician oversight will combine to improve care. We tested this assumption in the high-stakes diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum, a time-critical surgical emergency. In a multi-reader crossover study analyzing 1750 interpretation events, clinicians reviewed radiographs aided by either a high-reliability model or a systematically error-injected model. We found that high AI reliability paradoxically induces automation bias in trainees, who accepted 52.0% of incorrect suggestions, while offering limited gains to experts. Conversely, when challenged by flawed AI, the three participating neonatologists exhibited a “sentinel behavior” phenotype, correctly overriding 91.7% of errors (Wilson 95% CI: 83.0–96.0%) consistent with increased deliberation; given the small specialist cohort, this finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective replication. We operationalize systemic resilience as the capacity to maintain diagnostic integrity under algorithmic failure and demonstrate that clinical validity depends on the human–AI team’s adversarial resilience rather than standalone accuracy. To mitigate the risk of deskilling and never-skilling, we release an open-source educational sandbox designed to inoculate clinicians against automated errors.

title: GUARD-LGG: a glioma upfront AI-driven radiotherapy response decipher for lower-grade glioma
abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) remains a cornerstone in managing lower-grade glioma (LGG), but its response varies widely. Reliable pre-treatment prediction of RT response could facilitate patient management but remains unavailable. Here we present GUARD-LGG, a machine learning model designed to predict early RT response in LGG before treatment. GUARD-LGG was trained on 963 patients from a major center, tested on 187 patients from seven independent institutions, and 328 patients prospectively enrolled in a registered clinical trial. GUARD-LGG achieved AUCs of 0.946 (95% CI: 0.938–0.962), 0.929 (95% CI: 0.894–0.965), 0.882 (95% CI: 0.830–0.934), and 0.913 (95% CI: 0.878–0.949) in the training, internal validation, external, and prospective test sets, respectively. Model interpretation highlighted residual tumor, age, T2-weighted texture roughness and T1-weighted contrast intensity changes as major predictors. Radiogenomic analyses suggested potential associations between predicted unfavorable RT response and enrichment of RT resistance-related pathways. Consistently, patients with predicted unfavorable RT response exhibited shorter overall survival. In conclusion, GUARD-LGG enables individualized prediction of early RT response before therapy, offering a tool for pre-treatment response stratification in LGG.

title: MEDA-PKD: a dynamic, real-time analytics platform for precision care in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
authors: On behalf of the AD(H)PKD Study Group
abstract: The use of medical real-world data is constrained by fragmented data infrastructures and the absence of tools integrating longitudinal clinical with molecular data at scale. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), the most common monogenic cause of kidney failure, exemplifies this gap given its phenotypic complexity and the need for individualized treatment decisions. We present MEDA-PKD (MEdical DAta translation service of Polycystic Kidney Disease), an interactive, near-real-time analytics platform that integrates clinical routine with research data from the German AD(H)PKD Tolvaptan Registry (NCT02497521, DRKS00008910) into a harmonized database ( https://doi.org/10.18716/adpkd_registry ). MEDA-PKD provides automated near-real-time analysis and dynamic visualization, replacing traditional static approaches to clinical cohorts. As of March 2026, MEDA-PKD visualized data from 1735 patients (mean follow-up 796 days). eGFR slope analysis of data from patients initiating tolvaptan therapy (332 patients) demonstrates the platform’s capacity to evaluate real-world therapeutic impact in real-time. Other tabs include family history, medication, lifestyle, quality of life and a wide array of lab values (20,894 entries). Besides, MEDA-PKD integrates proteomics data and allows for secure individual patient-level data access. MEDA-PKD represents a paradigm shift by transforming static cohort data into a living, actionable knowledge resource in ADPKD and will serve as a template for other diseases.

title: Multi-site real-world performance of commercial AI for pulmonary and incidental pulmonary embolism detection
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs ( n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

title: Silent evaluation reveals context-dependent validity of automated metrics for AI-generated clinical messages
abstract: Evaluation of AI-generated patient communication lacks standardized frameworks, and automated metrics may not reflect clinical utility. We leveraged a staged rollout of GPT-generated draft responses (GDRs) to patient portal messages. Thirty primary care physicians received drafts from September 2023 to August 2024 under two conditions: an intervention group where AI drafts were displayed and edited ( n = 21,073), and a non-displayed group where drafts were generated but never shown to physicians, who composed responses independently ( n = 45,127). We evaluated messages using BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and Flesch Reading Ease, and then correlated automated metrics with blinded physician ratings of effectiveness, misunderstanding potential, and harm. In the intervention group, 2264 (11%) drafts were incorporated into final messages with high semantic alignment (BERTScore F1 = 0.93). In the non-displayed group, independent physician messages showed moderate similarity to unseen drafts (BERTScore F1 = 0.83). Despite comparable semantic scores, physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5). BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed. Automated metrics demonstrated context-dependent validity; they assessed editing fidelity but failed to evaluate whether AI-generated content matches independent human performance. Rigorous evaluation of clinical generative AI requires validation of metric meaning within specific use contexts.

title: A Generative AI-powered navigation system for precision CBCT-guided lung biopsies: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Lung puncture biopsy is the gold standard for the qualitative diagnosis of lung nodules. Cone Beam CT (CBCT) is commonly used for guiding punctures to locate lung nodules. However, the poor quality of CBCT images and the limited intelligence of surgical guidance systems have lowered the efficiency of puncture procedures, particularly for small and complex lesions. This study developed and validated a robust and accurate Generative AI-Powered Puncture Surgery Navigation System for lung punctures (GPS-Lung), demonstrating clinical applicability through a multicenter randomized controlled trial (Registration number: NCT06762613). The clinical results showed significant improvements in surgeon performance with the assistance of the integrated GPS-Lung system. Specifically, the system facilitated a more standardized and efficient operational process, reducing number of punctures (2.0 ± 1.2 vs. 2.5 ± 1.7, P = 0.005), shortening operative time (20.4 ± 5.6 min vs. 23.2 ± 6.3 min, P = 0.001), decreasing radiation exposure (4357.4 ± 3427.3 μGy·m 2 vs. 5570.9 ± 4846.7 μGy·m 2 , P = 0.033), and reducing pneumothorax complications (12.7% vs. 23.9%, P = 0.033). Taken together, the proposed system demonstrates promising clinical and translational value in lung nodule puncture intervention. (Clinical Trials Registration: NCT06762613). Clinical Trials Registration: NCT06762613, Registration Date: March 26, 2025. ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06762613?term=NCT06762613&rank=1&tab=history ).

title: Towards reliable morphological subtyping and cancer detection on Barrett’s esophagus pathology through ensembling foundation models
abstract: The reliability of emergent histopathology foundation models (Histo-FMs) for real-world diagnostic tasks remains unproven. Given the complexity of diagnostic tasks and the challenges inherent in real-world data, we utilized Histo-FMs to investigate their utility for morphological subtyping of Barrett’s esophagus (BE) and detecting esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) across the BE progression spectrum. We benchmarked Histo-FMs on the BarrettNet cohort, spanning diagnostic categories ranging from normal to EAC (N2EAC). The dataset comprised 3528 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) from 790 patients. A multi-magnification, multi-backbone aggregation of the five most expert-consistent single-scale models yielded incremental performance gains (AUROC of 0.907, F1-score of 0.696, accuracy of 0.795, and κ of 0.651 for morphological subtyping; AUROC of 0.909, F1-score of 0.836, accuracy of 0.959, and κ of 0.673 for EAC detection), with non-uniform gains across single-model comparisons and limited benefit for dysplasia. The findings support the capability of Histo-FMs for BE morphological subtyping and EAC detection in a multicenter clinical cohort, while highlighting persistent challenges in dysplasia assessment and the need for external validation. This study provides a foundation for future clinical validation.

title: A hybrid framework for Turner Syndrome facial detection: integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity
abstract: Turner Syndrome (TS) is a chromosomal disorder characterized by growth retardation and congenital ovarian dysgenesis. Given the considerable morbidity and mortality, early diagnosis and timely intervention are crucial to improving outcomes. However, the gold standard diagnostic method, karyotype analysis, is time-consuming and requires specialized laboratory expertise. Since TS patients often present distinct facial features, AI-based facial recognition could help identify patients with characteristic appearance as a screening tool. Inspired by the value-of-information principle, we propose a hybrid framework integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity. We retrospectively constructed this AI facial recognition model for TS detection and validated it in a prospective cohort. The proposed framework achieved 95.41% accuracy, 96.55% sensitivity, and 95.24% specificity, substantially simplifying the diagnostic process. When training was performed only on the hard subset obtained after difficulty-based stratification into three equal groups, the sensitivity reached 100.00%, indicating that all patients were correctly identified. Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions improved model interpretability and aligned predictions with clinical insights. Our method offers a low-cost and easily accessible approach to TS screening. By allowing for an earlier detection of TS, particularly in medical resource-limited settings, this method has the potential to facilitate timely interventions. This novel paradigm also provides insight for facial recognition-aided diagnosis in other diseases.

title: Multi-scale integration identifies an ox-LDL-autophagy-inflammasome framework linking osteoporosis and neurodegeneration
abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and neurodegeneration frequently co-occur with advancing age, but the biological processes linking skeletal and neurological decline remain incompletely understood. To investigate the metabolic-inflammatory axis connecting skeletal and neurological degeneration, we integrated cross-tissue multi-omics, single-cell transcriptomics, in vitro macrophage assays, and systems-level ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based modeling. Population-level and genetically informed analyses consistently implicated metabolic burden and lipid-associated stress in both disease domains, whereas physical activity showed protective associations. Cross-tissue and single-cell analyses identified convergent autophagy- and inflammasome-related programs, while cross-tissue multi-omics highlighted a PHF23-MCL1-CLN3 autophagy-associated molecular module. In RAW264.7 macrophages, oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) exposure induced inflammatory activation, pro-inflammatory polarization, and autophagy-associated dysregulation, while PHF23 perturbation modified ox-LDL-induced inflammatory responses. A 12-state ODE model further provided a hypothesis-generating representation of dynamic interactions among ox-LDL-associated metabolic stress, autophagy regulation, inflammasome activation, macrophage polarization, and tissue-damage-related states. Together, these multi-scale findings provide convergent support for an ox-LDL-autophagy-inflammasome-associated framework linking metabolic dysfunction with skeletal and neurological degeneration and generate testable hypotheses for further experimental investigation.

title: Large language models for multimodal clinical predictive modeling: a systematic review
abstract: The electronic health record (EHR) comprises structured and unstructured data, both of which are integral for comprehensively representing patient history. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has enabled the incorporation of unstructured data modalities into machine learning models that leverage EHR data. In this systematic review, we characterize studies that utilize LLM-enabled multimodal predictive modeling with EHR data. Following a screening of 641 studies, 57 met inclusion criteria. We identified three strategies for LLM-based multimodal integration: embedding, extraction, and text fusion. Delineated by the format of the unstructured data at the time of fusion, all strategies yielded performance gains (average 6.4% increase) over single modality models. LLMs facilitated modeling by generating note-embeddings for downstream prediction, extracting clinically informative variables, and summarizing long text documents prior to integration. Building on our review, we identified LLM-enhanced predictive modeling considerations that include sample size, interpretability, and computational costs. This study supports the potential value of LLMs for EHR-based predictive modeling and provides a framework for future multimodal modeling tools.

title: Clinical AI governance for scalable innovation in value based healthcare systems
abstract: Health systems are deploying clinical artificial intelligence (AI) faster than they can govern it, and existing frameworks emphasize risk oversight over operational learning and scale. The Collaborative Technology Adoption for Care Transformation (C-TACT) framework, developed at Southern California Permanente Medical Group (SCPMG), organizes governance across three pillars (People, Process, Technology) and four lifecycle stages (Vendor Evaluation, Pilot, Scale, Maintenance), each operationalized through a domain-weighted scorecard. Scale and Maintenance scorecards incorporate business and operational execution as weighted domains, with Analytic Hierarchy Process methods (consistency ratio 0.0037). In an illustrative, retrospective application, the Pilot Score Card separated two published SCPMG AI deployments and four anonymized comparators (47.0–53.5) by approximately thirty points across three weighting schemes. This separation illustrates how the framework behaves in this comparison. It is not evidence of validated discriminative performance, because the comparator scores were reconstructed retrospectively and were not scored under blinded conditions. C-TACT is presented here as a governance framework and a methodological demonstration. Prospective, blinded validation is needed to establish its discriminative and predictive performance under real-world conditions.

title: A deep learning framework for automated cervical spinal cord vertebral labeling and morphometric extraction from brain MRI with large-scale multicenter validation
abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a fully automated pipeline for vertebral level identification (C1–C3) of the upper cervical spinal cord (SC) in T1-weighted brain MRI with a quality control module to assess the generated masks. MRI data from 998 controls and 879 patients with hereditary ataxias (32 sites; age 5–85 years; 46% male) were used to train deep learning models (nnU-Net, U-Net with deep supervision, SwinUNETR) for automatic vertebral labeling of C1–C3 levels. A secondary model based on VGG, ResNet, and EfficientNet architectures was trained to identify vertebral labeling errors. The pipeline also generates image quality metrics including signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, coefficient of joint variation, and entropy focus criterion. External validation was performed using 2737 MRIs from four public datasets, and clinical utility was demonstrated in a longitudinal cohort of 51 patients with multiple sclerosis. The nnU-Net achieved the highest performance (Dice: C1 = 0.85, C2 = 0.89, C3 = 0.89), labeling 95.8% of mislabeled cases from the Spinal Cord Toolbox. The VGG-based classifier achieved 97.9% accuracy and 98.7% sensitivity. External validation showed labeling accuracies exceeding 92% in four of five datasets and sensitivity to longitudinal SC atrophy in multiple sclerosis. This pipeline enables scalable, reliable vertebral labeling and morphometric extraction of the upper cervical SC for multicenter studies and supports biomarker development in neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Technology-based structural racism and telehealth video usage among primary care patients
abstract: We tested whether technology-based structural racism mechanisms (digital redlining, path dependency, technical difficulties) were associated with lower telehealth video visit rates (versus audio-only; in-person visits excluded) among Black compared to White patients. Using structured and unstructured electronic health record data from 137,297 patients with completed telehealth visits over 26.5 months linked with broadband market data, we examined correlates of racial differences in video versus audio-only visits. Patient race had no significant unadjusted effect, but adjustment for individual and zip code level confounders revealed a 6% reduction in video visit rate ratios for Black patients, widening to 7–9% with interaction terms. For digital redlining, broadband market conditions were worse in areas with high neighborhood disadvantage and Black residential composition. However, broadband conditions were not associated with video visit rates. For path dependency, portal nonenrollment was more common among Black patients but had a stronger negative association with video visit rates among White patients. For technical difficulties, Black patients experienced more difficulties, which were associated with greater odds of a subsequent audio-only visit—particularly among Black patients. Findings suggest technology-based structural racism may operate through conditional and sequential mechanisms across telehealth stages. Health systems should monitor multilevel telehealth inequities across care stages.

title: From simulation to pedagogy: multi-model and randomized evaluation of structured AI standardized patients
abstract: Standardized patients (SPs) are central to clinical communication training but remain constrained by cost, scalability, and reliance on trained actors. We present AI standardized patients (AI-SPs), large language model–driven patient simulators built on a three-layer information architecture that adaptively modulates information disclosure according to learner skill. In Phase 1, blinded expert assessment of 350 simulated consultations generated by five frontier LLMs showed that, under a common architecture, learner skill level accounted for more of the observed performance variation than model choice ( η 2 = 0.31 vs. 0.06); whether this reflects the architecture itself cannot be determined without comparing models with and without it. In Phase 1b, analysis of 155 live student consultations identified systematic failures to elicit safety-critical information, enabling automated curriculum diagnostics without expert observation. In a Phase 2 three-arm pilot randomized study ( n = 58), OSCE performance gains with AI-SP training did not differ significantly from those with human SP training; the trial was designed to estimate effect sizes for a future confirmatory study, not to demonstrate equivalence. Self-efficacy gains were numerically largest with AI-SP training, but this exploratory difference did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. These findings suggest that architecture-driven AI-SPs could provide a scalable, model-portable approach to clinical communication training.

title: Human oversight of erroneous clinical AI and decision support a systematic review and meta analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports clinical decisions, but human oversight is protective only if clinicians recognize and resist erroneous output. We systematically reviewed controlled and real-world studies of clinician responses to incorrect automated advice. Forty-six reports represented 41 independent cohort clusters, including 40 core cohorts. Across three adjusted cohorts, clinician correctness was substantially higher with correct than incorrect automated advice (pooled OR 10.19, 95% CI 7.43–13.98; I² = 0%); a ≥ 2020 sensitivity analysis was similar but imprecise (OR 9.22, 95% CI 2.06–41.13). In four heterogeneous real-world computerized ECG studies, 26.6% of erroneous interpretations were not corrected or recognized (95% CI 6.4–65.6%; I² = 95.8%). Contemporary AI and large language model studies also documented harmful reliance but were too heterogeneous for pooling. Patient-level adverse events were reported in one retrospective cohort. Human oversight should be evaluated as an error-interception capability rather than assumed to ensure safety.

title: Systemwide adoption patterns of ambient AI scribe technology in an integrated academic health system
abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes may reduce documentation burden, but little is known about their adoption during enterprise-scale ambulatory rollout. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 2901 ambulatory clinicians at an integrated academic health system using linked electronic health record and vendor usage data from December 2024 through May 2025. Clinician adoption was defined as any use during the study period, and monthly visit-level uptake as the proportion of eligible ambulatory visits in which the ambient AI scribe was used. Adoption and uptake varied substantially across practice settings, specialties, and clinician types. Clinician-level adoption was highest in community internal medicine (67%), community general pediatrics (69%), and academic neurology (53%), and lowest in academic general surgery (16%), obstetrics and gynecology (18%), and psychiatry (19%). Community attending physicians and advanced practice providers showed marked increases in median visit-level uptake, reaching approximately 80%-90% in some groups by May 2025. Distinct longitudinal patterns included slow and steady adoption, early use followed by discontinuation, transient use, and late adoption. These findings suggest that implementation support and evaluation strategies should be tailored to local practice context rather than applied uniformly across a health system.

title: Visual-affective decoding enhances neurofunctional objective and generalizable signatures in unseen adolescent depression diagnosis
abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder is a highly prevalent and debilitating condition, yet objective and generalizable neurofunctional signatures remain elusive. Existing neuroimaging approaches largely rely on resting-state fMRI, or controlled tasks often lack ecological validity and generalizable signatures of depression-related neural dysfunctions. This study proposes a Visual–Affective Decoding (VAD) framework integrating cross-subject visual and affective decoding from whole-brain fMRI acquired during naturalistic movie viewing. A dual-pathway anomaly detection model trained exclusively on healthy controls establishes normative brain function and identifies MDD through deviations from this norm. In 200 adolescents (112 MDD, 88 HC), VAD achieved an AUC of 0.87, 95.56% sensitivity, 83.89% accuracy, and 72.22% specificity. Using the same anomaly threshold, it generalized to an independent external adolescent cohort (70 MDD, 68 HC), achieving an AUC of 0.81 with an accuracy of 75.36%, supporting its cross-site generalizability. VAD further revealed interpretable neurofunctional signatures, including blunted emotional reactivity, attenuated visual representation, and affective patterns consistent with emotional rumination. Region-level contribution analyses identified dissociable visual- and affective-sensitive cortical regions, consistent with dysfunctions in visual, default-mode, salience, and higher-order associative networks. These findings demonstrate that VAD provides objective, interpretable, and generalizable neurofunctional signatures for adolescent depression diagnosis and clinically relevant biomarker development.

title: Multicentre benchmark of PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI fusion for non-invasive clinically significant prostate cancer diagnosis
abstract: Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) guides-biopsy and treatment decisions, yet its non-invasive diagnosis remains challenging. The incremental value of PSMA PET/CT beyond multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and the optimal strategy for multimodal fusion, remain unclear.
